title: How to Buy Pay Per Call Leads (Inbound Calls)
h1: How to buy pay per call leads and inbound calls
description: Want to buy pay per call leads? Learn how to buy inbound calls, set your rules for a billable call, test quality, and pay only for calls that convert.
faq: What does it mean to buy pay per call leads?

It means paying for live inbound phone calls instead of clicks or form fills. A publisher or network sends you callers who match your rules, and you pay a set price for each call that qualifies — for example one that reaches your minimum call duration from an allowed state.
How much do pay per call leads cost?

It varies by vertical and caller quality. High-intent calls in legal, insurance or home services cost more than general enquiries. Most buyers agree a price per qualified call with the publisher, and some use real-time bidding so the price reflects what each call is worth.
Where can I buy inbound calls?

From pay per call networks, marketplaces, or directly from publishers who generate calls in your vertical. Start with a small daily cap to test quality, review the recordings, then scale the sources that convert for you.
body:
Buying pay per call leads means paying for live phone calls from people who want what you sell, rather than for clicks, impressions or form fills that may never pick up the phone. You agree what a good call looks like, a publisher sends you callers that match, and you pay per call that qualifies. Done well it is one of the highest-intent channels there is; done carelessly you pay for hang-ups. Here is how to buy inbound calls the right way.

What you are actually buying

A pay per call lead is a real inbound call from someone with intent — a homeowner who needs a roof fixed, a caller comparing insurance, a person asking about a legal claim. You pay a price for each call that meets your rules, not for every call that rings. That is the whole appeal: your cost lines up with callers who are ready to talk, and you can hear the quality for yourself in the recording.

Where to buy pay per call leads

  • Networks and marketplaces — the fastest start. The buyers, publishers, prices and rules are already in place, so you can test a vertical quickly.
  • Direct from publishers — higher quality control and often a better price once you know which sources convert, in exchange for doing the vetting yourself.
  • Through a call platform — if you run volume across several publishers, a platform lets you set one set of rules and see every call in one place.

New to the model? Our guide to what pay per call is explains how publishers, affiliates and buyers fit together.

Set your rules before you buy

The buyers who do well decide what a billable call is before they spend a cent. Agree these in writing:

  1. States and regions you are licensed or able to serve.
  2. Opening hours and a daily cap so calls arrive when you can answer them.
  3. Minimum call duration — the seconds a call must last to count. See minimum call duration explained.
  4. Duplicate rules so you are not charged twice for the same caller. See duplicate calls in pay per call.

How to test quality before you scale

Start small. Set a low daily cap, take calls for a week, and listen to the recordings instead of trusting a dashboard alone. Track how many calls turned into real conversations and sales, work out your cost per sale, and only then raise the cap on the sources that pay off. A caller who hangs up in ten seconds is not a lead, and a clear minimum duration plus recordings is how you keep those off your invoice.
